articleTitle: Crosstalk on low-traffic channels A probabilistic approach
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The subject of rural telephone provision is of great current interest. Such a service is costly to provide in relation to the traffic that it carries so that it can be difficult to justify on purely economic grounds. Often, considerable extra costs are incurred in upgrading elementary facilities to bring crosstalk up to the standards expected of normal urban or business systems. This note considers the small expected duration of crosstalk within any call period and, accepting that even brief intelligible crosstalk is untenable, discusses possible alternative strategies.

articleTitle: An investigation of sequence discriminators used as wide-band quadrature phase shift networks
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Sequence discriminators have been proposed for use as wide-band quadrature phase shift networks. This article briefly describes the operation of these networks, and derives an expression for the phase shift of a simple RC sequence discriminator. Equiripple quadrature phase shift networks were designed using this expression, and their actual responses compared against the theory. A set of design curves giving equal phase error off quadrature for different bandwidths and network sizes is presented. The sensitivity of these networks were investigated using Monte Carlo analysis and the results summarised. On the basis of these results, a design rule giving the least sensitive network configuration is presented. An active variation of the network is investigated and shown to have a far lower sensitivity.

articleTitle: Electric shark-barrier: Power-electronics
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The traditional method or protecting bathing beaches from sporadic shark-attack is reviewed in terms of its problematic efficacy and environmental incompatibility. The shark-repellent electric-barrier concept capable of overcoming these problems is reviewed. An experimental application of the barrier for the purpose of determining field strengths and electrode-cable endurance under conditions of 2 to 3 m sand movement is described. The results demonstrate that the minimum field-strengths necessary to repel sharks can be maintained. The range over which the field strength varies along the length of the barrier, on the water surface, was from a low of 4 V/m in deep water to 14 V/m in shallow water. The electrode-system offers a high ratio of inductive reactance to resistance at its terminals. A method of efficiently producing large current pulses in such a load is described.

articleTitle: A novel planar double balanced image recovery mixer
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The design of a double balanced image recovery mixer is described. The mixer features a fully planar implementation of the wide band RF and LO baluns. The conversion loss of the mixer is less than 3, 5 dB, and the image rejection better than 15 dB. With an IF amplifier noise figure of 2.0 dB, the overall mixer noise figure was 4.8 dB. Die ontwerp van 'n dubbel-gebalanseerde beeldherwinningsmenger word bespreek. Die menger is van planêre konstruksie. Die omsettingsverlies van die menger is minder as 3,5 dB, en die beeldverwerping meer as 15 dB. Met 'n tussenfrekwensieversterker met 'n ruissyfer van 2 dB, is die ruissyfer van die menqer 4.8 dB.

articleTitle: Development of a three-phase variable speed drive system for a battery fed underground mining locomotive
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Small locomotives are extensively used in South African mines for transporting material from the mining face to the tip. These are typically 4 to 10 tons in weight. The majority of them are used in gold mines at depths down to almost 4000 meters.

articleTitle: Industrial application of a real-time expert system
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The successful implementation of a real-time expert system on an industrial chemical plant was managed as a collaborative project. After investigation of knowledge requirements, a rule-based knowledge representation language was defined and the expert system implemented using the POPLOG development environment. The final expert system provided recipe recommendations to the operator of the batch plant. Extensive evaluation was performed on the system.

articleTitle: The reduction of bias in passive range estimation
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Filtering in nonlinear situations leads generally to biased estimates. Probably the simplest example for electrical engineers is the rectification-filtering of 50 Hz AC to “biased” DC. While a general theoretical treatment of this problem cannot be included here, we exploit the practical problem of passive range tracking of a moving source, to demonstrate how to significantly reduce bias in an essentially nonlinear application of (Kalman) filtering. The essence of our (not universally applicable) approach is: formulate the measurements in a (if necessary artificial) linear form and filter only linear relationships by “shifting” all non–linearities into additive system disturbance terms.

articleTitle: The modelling of terrain irregularities as applied in field strength prediction techniques
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The paper presents a selection of models for paths and separate obstacles which have been successfully used by the South African Broadcasting Corporation (SABC) for field strength prediction in VHF and UHF broadcasting. The models are recommended and used by various organisations such as the CCIR (International Radio Consultive Committee), EBU (European Broadcasting Union) and BBC (British Broadcasting Corporation). This particular selection is intended to be used with terrain data derived from maps preferably with a scale of 1:50000 or better. The methods based on these models are appropriate for long-term free-space, interference and diffraction field strength prediction.

articleTitle: High performance, matched, double pole, double throw UHF switch
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper describes the development and design of high performance, matched, double pole, double throw UHF PIN diode switches. It features very small reflection coefficients at all four ports in both switch states with low insertion loss and high isolation. The switch design is based on a compact distributed filter, resulting in small size for the realized performance.

articleTitle: Markov chain model of a line coded data stream
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The paper presents a new concept of the general Markov–Chain model for a line coded data, found directly from the code's tabular description, It incorporates both Moore's and Mealy's representations of a code in a sense that, it is easily reducible to each of them. The model is applicable to the cases of independent and correlated input data. It is valid for both fixed and variable word length codes used in the high speed digital communication systems. The discussed concepts are well illustrated via their application to the AMI, AMI-III and HDB-3 codes.

articleTitle: A two frequency inverter for fluorescent lamps
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper covers the work performed for an Electronic Engineering final year undergraduate project. A DC to AC inverter for fluorescent lamps was designed and constructed. The inverter employed resonant elements and operated first at one frequency, to preheat the lamp cathodes, then at the resonant frequency of the circuit, for starting and running of the lamp. Important design factors were the efficiency of energy conversion from electrical input to light output, and the cost-effectiveness of the electronic circuitry. A prototype circuit was constructed and was found to perform to the satisfaction of the sponsors.

articleTitle: An expert system for controller design
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: An intelligent tool for the design of linear control systems has been built by combining an expert system with a recently developed numerical design technique. The expert system assists the designer in formulating a comprehensive and achievable specification, and in dealing with any constraint conflicts which may arise. The use of the design system by undergraduate students is also examined.

articleTitle: Exploiting the capacity of the discrete input restricted channel
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Coding schemes for the (d,k) = (1,2), (1,4), (2,3) and (2,4) discrete input restricted channels are presented. These coding schemes incorporate an ancillary channel for better utilization of the capacity of the (d,k) input restricted channel. A matrix method for the computation of the above mentioned capacity is shown The synthesis of coding schemes without and with the ancillary channel is presented. Error propagation and error probability behaviour were investigated by simulation and the results are presented.

articleTitle: The effect of air density on the impulse characteristics of wood pole insulation
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The influence of air density on the lightning impulse level of wood pole lines where wood forms part of the main insulation has been investigated by conducting lightning impulse tests in two laboratories with a 1500 m altitude difference. The test results for wood samples alone indicate an air correction factor of the same order as that of an air gap. In the case of an insulator in series with the wood a three per cent lower correction factor applies. This phenomenon is explained with reference to different flashover mechanisms. The moisture content of the wood and the surface moisture however have an overriding effect. It is therefore recommended that no air density correction be applied in impulse tests on wood pole lines.

articleTitle: A simplified technique for analyzing loaded broadband wire antennas
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: A non-uniform transmission line model of thick, loaded wire antennas was developed for their rapid analysis over a wide frequency range. Both a lossless line, with radiation effects modelled as a termination impedance, and a lossy line with radiation accounted for by series resistance were investigated. Input impedance and radiation efficiency results over a 10:1 frequency range are presented for thick loaded dipoles. These results indicate that the lossy line technique is suitable for the design and evaluation of loaded dipoles. The time to analyse electrically long dipoles is reduced by orders of magnitude in comparison with Method of Moments procedures.

articleTitle: Three-phase transistor inverter for low voltage, high current, battery fed applications
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The paper summarises development work on a three phase pwm inverter using large bipolar power transistors and a direct base drive technique. The base drive technology, turn–on and turn-off snubbing, reverse conduction at turn–on, component ratings and lay–out considerations are covered. The described prototype has been designed for a 84V, 350A rating.

articleTitle: An accurate model for the simulation of the deep bar effect in induction motors
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The paper gives a lumped parameter circuit to be used in modelling the deep bar effects in rotors of induction motors. This circuit is obtained by dividing the rotor bar into equal sections; an improvement is proposed which divides the bar unequally to have a greater number of smaller sections at the top of the bar where the current will flow under transient conditions. An example shows the superiority of this model compared to the traditional induction motor model.

articleTitle: A hybrid system for digital image data compression
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: In this paper a two dimensional hybrid coder is presented. The coder has performance comparable to that of the Discrete Cosine Transform while using a reduced blocksize for transformation. This makes it especially suitable for real time implementation. The discussion closes with the results from objective and subjective evaluations of the algorithm.

articleTitle: Human response to pulsed electric fields in sea-water
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The accepted 50/60 Hz current, human electro-physiological threshold responses of feeling, let-go, difficult breathing, fibrillation & convulsions are reviewed, Similar response thresholds are required for the safe design of electrical shark repellents where the relevant parameter measured in sea-water is volt per metre. An experiment is described which hypothesizes a simple proportional relationship between the two sets of electrical conditions. This involves the use of a single test subject as a “transfer standard” between the two. The transfer coefficient was determined at the threshold of feeling and used to predict where the let-go threshold field strength in sea-water should lie. The equivalent ‘let-go’ threshold case was determined. This estimate confirmed the predicted value. The same proportional relationship is consequently applied to indicate the threshold field strength at which difficult breathing, fibrillation and convulsions may occur. Useful data on 50 Hz fields in sea-water is also derived.

articleTitle: The challenge of intelligent computing
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The pace and complexity of modern society and industry place stringent demands on all kinds of automation systems. A possible approach for finding timely solutions to the resulting problems is through the use of intelligent computing and knowledge systems. This paper explores the concept of intelligent computing and its associated benefits. The exacting requirements that knowledge systems of the future must meet to become functional and useful engineering tools are identified.

articleTitle: The use of fuzzy sets theory for modelling complex processes
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: A theory is developed in which the coefficients of a differential equation that represents a physical process are expressed as fuzzy sets, rather than as exact numerical values. Given an input, which may or may not be fuzzy, the differential equation can then be solved to yield an output fuzzy set. In order to achieve this, the mathematical operations on fuzzy sets are redefined because many of the required properties do not hold when using existing theories.

articleTitle: Superconductive three-terminal devices utilizing quasiparticle tunneling
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The characteristics of a family of three-terminal superconductive devices, which utilizes the tunneling of quasiparticles, are described. The current-voltage characteristics of these devices are illustrated by computer simulation results.

articleTitle: Non-equilibrium quasiparticle processes in superconductor tunneling structures
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: A broad overview is presented of the phenomenon of superconductivity. The tunneling of quasiparticles in superconductor-insulator structures is described. Related non-equilibrium processes, such as superconductor bandgap suppression, quasiparticle diffusion and recombination, and excess quasiparticle collection are discussed. The processes are illustrated with numerical computer simulation data. The importance of the inter-relationship between these processes in practical multiple tunneling junction superconducting device structures is also emphasized.

articleTitle: Analysis of radio refractivity data and some implications for frequency management
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The influence of atmospheric variables on the radio refractive index is discussed. The distribution of the atmospheric refractive index in time and space influences radio system planning through it's effect on the effective earth radius and hence the received signal strength, wanted or interfering. It is suggested that standard practice in relating the effective earth radius to the refractivity gradient over the first kilometre of the troposphere may not be appropriate in all cases and that this has implications for frequency management and radio system planning.

articleTitle: Throughput capacity of meteor burst communications
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: A great deal of recent interest has been focussed on data communications by meteor burst, and a number of theoretical models of such communications have been derived. This paper describes results obtained from practical monitoring systems using midpath and endpath meteor burst links. Data captured by these systems is used to simulate the throughput capacity of the links, and the results are compared with those of simulations based on the theoretical models. Results of both fixed and adaptive bit rate systems are discussed and compared. In addition, the relative contributions of the various trail families to channel capacity are discussed in some depth.

articleTitle: Accurate numerical procedures for the synthesis of microwave filters
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The development of a fully interactive and virtually foolproof software package for the accurate approximation and synthesis of discrete and distributed element filters of high order and narrow bandwidth, is discussed. The network elements accommodated in the synthesis are the Darlington A, B and C sections and the commensurate quarter wavelength transmission line element. Nearly all filters required for a specified amplitude frequency response may be designed with these elements. The developed software runs on IBM and compatible microcomputers equipped with a 8086 processor and 8087 mathematical coprocessor. Die ontwikkeling van qebruikersvriendelike interaktiewe programmatuur vir die akkurate benadering en sintese van punt- en verspreideelement filters word bespreek. Die filters wat hiermee ontwerp word, bestaan uit 'n kombinasie van Darlington A, B en C - seksies, en die kwartgolflengte transmissieelement. Byna alle filters wat vir 'n gegewe amplitude-frekwensieweergawe gespesifiseer word, kan met hierdie elemente gerealiseer word. Die program is geskik vir IBM en versoenbare persoonlike rekenaars wat toegerus moet wees met 'n 8087 wiskundige koverwerker.

articleTitle: Hardware and software development of a personal computer based distortion measuring system in a three phase power supply
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: An instrument capable of performing time-domain electrical power analysis is proposed and practical results achieved with it are presented. Moderate cost was one of the main criteria as there are several dedicated instruments, currently available, at high costs, which could compete with several of the features provided by this unit. The design of the TDPMI (Time Domain Power Measuring Instrument) has however been optimized for power system measurements and is linked to a host personal computer. The personal computer performs the signal processing and mathematical analysis, while the hardware system performs the data acquisition. This technical note further describes some of the on-line operational characteristics of this measurement system which has excellent industrialization prospects.

articleTitle: Service experience with SF6 gas insulated switchgear in Southern Africa
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Details of SF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf> GIS installations in service in Southern Africa from 1977 up to 1986 are presented including quantitative data of components and operating service. The various types of failures that have occurred in service are listed together with quantitative data on failure events and rates for GIS and associated circuit breakers and comparisons with previously published failure rates. Analysis of the change in failure rates with years of service and failures against basic causes are given. Comments are presented on enclosure failure and pressure relief events, gas leakage, disconnecting switch performance and scheduled maintenance.

articleTitle: The development of a LQG controller design procedure
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: An adaptive LQG control algorithm for SISO systems has been successfully implemented on a personal computer. The parameters of a CARIMA model are found using a staged recursive estimation algorithm. The LQG controller is designed based upon this model, and controller bandwidth can be tuned on-line. Several engineering features were added to ensure reliable parameter and state estimation. The program was tested in real time and produced good results. Simulations further showed that the resulting controllers were insensitive to incorrect assumptions of model order and delay.

articleTitle: An investigation of forward error correcting codes for a meteor burst communication channel
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Meteor Burst Communication Links offer the facility for transmitting data via trails of ionised particles, which form continually as meteors enter our atmosphere. Unfortunately, this propagation medium is exposed to countless external disturbances, and is therefore inherently noisy. Most commercial systems have overcome this difficulty by means of Automatic Repeat Request (AHQ) protocols, where received frames containing errors are simply retransmitted. This paper investigates the viability of an alternative system, viz. the Forward Error Correcting (FEC) protocol, where sufficient redundancy is inserted at the transmitter to enable correction of the noise-corrupted bits by the receiver. An accurate simulation of the complete link was implemented in software (C), effectively modelling the encoding, modulation, noise-corruption, demodulation and decoding processes. Four coding schemes were examined (Reed-Solomon, Golay, Viterbi and Iwadare), and comprehensive testing was performed using live trail data. Analyses of our results and tentative conclusions are presented.

articleTitle: A simple continuous multiparabolic model of ionospheric electron density distribution for use in certain hf communications applications
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This work describes the development of a multiparabolic (MP) ionospheric model and compares the results at vertical incidence with those of the equivalent Dudeney model in the absence of the geomagnetic field. The MP model is extended to a multi-quasiparabolic (MQP) model in order to obtain analytical expressions for the variation of communications range as a function of elevation angle in the absence of the geomagnetic field and collisions. Results compare very favourably with those obtained using the equivalent Dudeney model and numerical ray-tracing. The MQP model can be applied in a number of HF communications problems, notably single site location HF direction finding and HF ionospheric radar.

articleTitle: Phase-to-phase air insulation studies under ambient conditions of reduced air density
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: In this paper the results of a series of phase-to-phase switching impulse tests in a 4 m horizontal rod-rod gap and a 4 m parallel conductor-conductor gap are presented. The tests were performed outdoors at an altitude of 1 550 m using two conventional Marx-circuit switching impulse generators. The positive 50% disruptive discharge voltage in each gap is reported for waveshapes of 250/2 500 us and 160/1 800 μs and a range of α-factors (defined according to IEC recommendations as α = U<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">–</sup>/(U<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">–</sup> + U<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup>)) of 0, 0,33 and 0,5 - the negative impulses having constant synchronous times-to-crest of 2 000 μs. Measurements of the apparent charge injected at both positive and negative electrodes are reported and the effect of pre-existing negative space charge on the positive leader development and the resultant reduction in breakdown voltage are briefly discussed, with special reference to conditions of reduced relative air density (δ = 0.85).
